punchline: An American engineer's largely ignored idea helped spark Japan's post-war quality revolution.
thirty_sec: Richard Koch describes how Pareto's principle was largely ignored until quality expert Joseph Juran applied it to manufacturing: a vital few causes produced most defects. His ideas attracted little interest in the United States, so after the Second World War he worked with Japanese industry, which embraced them. Koch credits this as part of the Japanese quality revolution. The lesson: find the vital few and fix them first.
question: Which few problems are causing most of your trouble?
